nodes.name: Pamir grasses
nodes.desc: Wheatgrasses and related grasses are among the commonly recorded plants of the high Pamir steppe and feed grazers.

nodes.name: Sedges
nodes.desc: Sedges grow in damp alpine ground; Wikipedia notes sedges are a main food of argali and of ibex in spring and summer.

nodes.name: Pamirian winterfat
nodes.desc: A low, hardy shrub of dry mountain steppe and one of the most recorded plants near the park.

nodes.name: Oxytropis
nodes.desc: Cushion-forming legumes of stony alpine ground, well recorded near the park, that give grazers protein-rich forage.

nodes.name: Tien Shan birch
nodes.desc: A shrubby birch of sheltered Pamir valleys, one of the few tree-like plants in the park.

nodes.name: Marco Polo sheep
nodes.desc: The Pamir argali is the largest argali race. Argali eat grasses, sedges and forbs and are hunted mainly by wolves and snow leopards.

nodes.name: Siberian ibex
nodes.desc: A cliff-dwelling goat of steep, rocky ground above the tree line. It eats alpine grasses and herbs, and twigs in winter.

nodes.name: Long-tailed marmot
nodes.desc: A burrowing herbivore of alpine meadow and steppe that hibernates from about September to spring.

nodes.name: Himalayan snowcock
nodes.desc: A large mountain game bird, the most recorded bird near the park, living on high rocky slopes and meadows.

nodes.name: Horned Lark
nodes.desc: A small ground bird of open, bare alpine and steppe ground that eats seeds and insects.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: A small hunter of burrows and open ground. GloBI records it eating small birds such as horned larks.

nodes.name: Yellow-billed chough
nodes.desc: A flocking mountain crow that forages on the ground for seeds and invertebrates and scavenges around human camps.

nodes.name: Bearded vulture
nodes.desc: A scavenger whose diet is mostly bone and marrow from the carcasses of mid-sized hoofed animals, which it drops to crack open.

nodes.name: Snow leopard
nodes.desc: An elusive cat that preys on wild sheep and goats such as argali and ibex, and also on marmots and other small mammals.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: Wikipedia calls Himalayan wolves the main predator of argali, taking animals of any age, especially in deep winter snow.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A large raptor of crags and open slopes. GloBI records it eating marmots and stoats; argali lamb remains have been found in nests.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong high-altitude sunlight drives the short summer growing season.

nodes.name: Glacial meltwater
nodes.desc: Glaciers such as Fedchenko feed streams and wet meadows in a very dry climate.

nodes.name: Thin rocky soil
nodes.desc: Cold, dry, stony soils hold few nutrients and recycle them slowly.

nodes.name: Soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil, slowly in the cold.
